code: # a half-sib design: 12 sires, 2 dams each, 6 offspring per pair nsire <- 12; ndam_per <- 2; noff <- 6 nfound <- nsire + nsire * ndam_per n <- nfound + nsire * ndam_per * noff ped <- data.frame(id = 1:n, sire = NA_integer_, dam = NA_integer_) k <- nfound for (s in 1:nsire) for (j in 1:ndam_per) {   dam <- nsire + ndam_per * (s - 1) + j   for (o in 1:noff) { k <- k + 1; ped$sire[k] <- s; ped$dam[k] <- dam } }  # the tabular method builds A from a pedigree sorted parents-first A <- diag(n) for (i in seq_len(n)) {   s <- ped$sire[i]; d <- ped$dam[i]   if (!is.na(s)) {     A[i, i] <- 1 + 0.5 * A[s, d]     for (j in seq_len(i - 1)) A[i, j] <- A[j, i] <- 0.5 * (A[j, s] + A[j, d])   } } dimnames(A) <- list(as.character(ped$id), as.character(ped$id))  set.seed(9) dat <- data.frame(id = factor(ped$id, levels = ped$id),                   sex = factor(rep(c("f", "m"), length.out = n))) # additive genetic values with sd 1, residual sd 1, so h2 = 0.5 dat$phen <- 5 + 0.4 * (dat$sex == "m") +   as.numeric(t(chol(A)) %*% rnorm(n)) + rnorm(n, 0, 1) fit <- frm(bf(phen ~ sex + (1 | gr(id, cov = A))) + gaussian(),            data = dat, data2 = list(A = A), REML = TRUE,            control = frmtmb_control(check_olre = "ignore")) sd_a <- sqrt(VarCorr(fit)[[1]][1, 1]) c(sd_additive = sd_a, sigma = sigma(fit),   heritability = sd_a^2 / (sd_a^2 + sigma(fit)^2)) #>  sd_additive        sigma heritability  #>    0.9058984    1.0139575    0.4438927

what: Cross-check against the closed-form REML likelihood
title: Case studies: models from the showcase literature
text: gaussian animal model marginal distribution known closed form: y ~ N(X beta, sd_a^2 + sigma^2 ). restricted log likelihood model can written six lines maximized optim(). uses part frmtmb. variance components restricted log likelihood agree six significant digits.
code: X <- model.matrix(~ sex, dat); y <- dat$phen nll <- function(p) {   V <- exp(p[1]) * A + exp(p[2]) * diag(n)   Vi <- solve(V); M <- crossprod(X, Vi) %*% X   b <- solve(M, crossprod(X, Vi) %*% y); r <- y - X %*% b   as.numeric(0.5 * ((n - ncol(X)) * log(2 * pi) + determinant(V)$modulus +                       determinant(M)$modulus + crossprod(r, Vi %*% r))) } op <- optim(c(0, 0), nll, method = "BFGS", control = list(reltol = 1e-13)) out <- rbind(frmtmb = c(sd_a, sigma(fit), as.numeric(logLik(fit))),              closed_form = c(sqrt(exp(op$par)), -op$value)) colnames(out) <- c("sd_additive", "sigma", "restricted_logLik") out #>             sd_additive    sigma restricted_logLik #> frmtmb        0.9058984 1.013958         -300.9229 #> closed_form   0.9058980 1.013958         -300.9229

code: bcg <- data.frame(   tpos = c(4, 6, 3, 62, 33, 180, 8, 505, 29, 17, 186, 5, 27),   tneg = c(119, 300, 228, 13536, 5036, 1361, 2537, 87886, 7470, 1699,            50448, 2493, 16886),   cpos = c(11, 29, 11, 248, 47, 372, 10, 499, 45, 65, 141, 3, 29),   cneg = c(128, 274, 209, 12619, 5761, 1079, 619, 87892, 7232, 1600,            27197, 2338, 17825),   ablat = c(44, 55, 42, 52, 13, 44, 19, 13, 27, 42, 18, 33, 33)) bcg$yi <- log((bcg$tpos / (bcg$tpos + bcg$tneg)) /                 (bcg$cpos / (bcg$cpos + bcg$cneg))) bcg$vi <- 1 / bcg$tpos - 1 / (bcg$tpos + bcg$tneg) +   1 / bcg$cpos - 1 / (bcg$cpos + bcg$cneg) bcg$sei <- sqrt(bcg$vi) bcg$study <- factor(seq_len(nrow(bcg))) fmeta <- frm(bf(yi | se(sei) ~ 1 + (1 | study)) + gaussian(),              data = bcg, REML = TRUE) c(pooled_logRR = unname(fixef(fmeta)$mu), se = sqrt(vcov(fmeta)[1, 1]),   tau = sqrt(VarCorr(fmeta)[[1]][1, 1])) #> pooled_logRR           se          tau  #>   -0.7145323    0.1804360    0.5596814 pooled <- unname(fixef(fmeta)$mu) tinyplot::tinyplot(yi ~ study, data = bcg,                    ymin = bcg$yi - 1.96 * bcg$sei,                    ymax = bcg$yi + 1.96 * bcg$sei,                    type = "pointrange", flip = TRUE, theme = "clean2",                    col = "black", pch = 16,                    xlab = "study", ylab = "log risk ratio") abline(v = pooled, lty = 2, col = "firebrick") abline(v = 0, lty = 3, col = "gray50") confint_varcorr(fmeta) #>       block        term type  estimate       lwr       upr #> 1 1 | study (Intercept)   sd 0.5596814 0.3310656 0.9461668

code: rr <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = bcg, method = "REML") out <- rbind(frmtmb = c(unname(fixef(fmeta)$mu), sqrt(vcov(fmeta)[1, 1]),                         sqrt(VarCorr(fmeta)[[1]][1, 1])),              metafor = c(as.numeric(rr$beta), rr$se, sqrt(rr$tau2))) colnames(out) <- c("pooled_logRR", "se", "tau") out #>         pooled_logRR        se       tau #> frmtmb    -0.7145323 0.1804360 0.5596814 #> metafor   -0.7145323 0.1797815 0.5596815 stopifnot(   abs(fixef(fmeta)$mu - as.numeric(rr$beta)) < 1e-5,   abs(sqrt(VarCorr(fmeta)[[1]][1, 1]) - sqrt(rr$tau2)) < 1e-5,   # the standard errors come from different expressions: metafor uses   # (X'WX)^-1 at the REML tau, frmtmb reads the joint Hessian   abs(sqrt(vcov(fmeta)[1, 1]) / rr$se - 1) < 0.01 )

title: Likelihood-ratio tests between nested frmtmb fits — anova.frmtmb_fit
code: set.seed(1) n <- 200 dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n), g = factor(rep(1:20, 10))) u <- cbind(rnorm(20, 0, 0.8), rnorm(20, 0, 0.5)) dd$y <- rnorm(n, 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 1] + u[dd$g, 2] * dd$x, 1)  m0 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) m1 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) anova(m0, m1) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                     Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq) #> y ~ x + (1 | g)      4 -334.52 677.04                          #> y ~ x + z + (1 | g)  5 -334.05 678.10 0.9394      1     0.3324  # dropping a variance component puts the null on the boundary, so # this p-value is conservative by up to a factor of two m2 <- frm(bf(y ~ x) + gaussian(), data = dd) anova(m2, m0) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                 Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq)     #> y ~ x            3 -352.75 711.51                              #> y ~ x + (1 | g)  4 -334.52 677.04 36.468      1  1.552e-09 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1  # REML fits compare only when the fixed-effect designs agree, which # is the case for a variance-component test r0 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) r1 <- frm(bf(y ~ x + (x | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) anova(r0, r1) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                 Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq)     #> y ~ x + (1 | g)  2 -336.69 677.39                              #> y ~ x + (x | g)  4 -325.44 658.87 22.516      2   1.29e-05 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 # differing designs are refused; refit = TRUE compares ML fits instead rz <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, REML = TRUE) try(anova(r0, rz)) #> Error : REML likelihoods are comparable only between fits whose fixed-effect designs span the same column space; these do not. Pass refit = TRUE (or refit with REML = FALSE) to compare fixed effects, or hold the fixed effects fixed to compare random-effect structures anova(r0, rz, refit = TRUE) #> anova(): refitting 2 REML models with ML: y ~ x + (1 | g); y ~ x + z + (1 | g) #> Likelihood-ratio tests #>  #>                     Df  logLik    AIC  Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq) #> y ~ x + (1 | g)      4 -334.52 677.04                          #> y ~ x + z + (1 | g)  5 -334.05 678.10 0.9394      1     0.3324

title: Pooled model comparison across imputations (D1, D2, D3) — anova.frmtmb_multiple
text: "D1" Multivariate Wald (Li, Raghunathan Rubin 1991). Let Qbar pooled estimate k coefficients larger model adds, Ubar average within-imputation covariance B -imputation covariance. average relative increase variance r, (1 + 1/m) tr(B Ubar^-1) / k, statistic Qbar' ((1 + r) Ubar)^-1 Qbar / k k v degrees freedom. v uses Reiter (2007) small-sample form dfcom finite Li et al form otherwise. "D2" Pooled test statistics (Li, Meng, Raghunathan Rubin 1991). m per-imputation statistics d - either likelihood-ratio chi-squares (use = "likelihood") Wald chi-squares (use = "wald") - r set (1 + 1/m) var(sqrt(d)), statistic (mean(d)/k - (m + 1)/(m - 1) r) / (1 + r) k k^(-3/m) (m - 1) (1 + 1/r)^2 degrees freedom. D2 needs covariance matrix, cheapest rule least efficient. "D3" Pooled likelihood ratio (Meng Rubin 1992). average deviance difference computed twice: imputation-specific estimates (dbar) pooled estimates (dtilde), second evaluating imputation's likelihood one common parameter vector. r set (m + 1) / (k (m - 1)) (dbar - dtilde), statistic dtilde / (k (1 + r)). D3 default: needs covariance matrix either, unlike D2 stays valid coefficients far normal. Pooled parameter values plain across-imputation means optimizer's parameter vector, variance components pooled internal (log / Cholesky) scale, matching $pooled. model refit: imputation's objective re-evaluated pooled vector, costs one Laplace solve. mice::D3() instead fixes pooled coefficients offset re-estimates every remaining parameter, can differ percent; mitml::testModels(method = "D3") uses plug-form implemented . Note also df.residual() counts dispersion parameter gaussian fit, lm() , dfcom one smaller mice's default; pass dfcom explicitly reproduce mice exactly.

title: Check a custom family's log-density for AD safety — check_custom_family
code: set.seed(1) y <- rpois(50, 3)  # a hand-written poisson: check it before fitting anything with it ok <- custom_family(   "my_poisson", dpars = "mu", links = list(mu = "log"),   lpdf = function(y, dpars, aterms) {     y * log(dpars$mu) - dpars$mu - lgamma(y + 1)   },   type = "discrete" ) check_custom_family(ok, y = y, dpars = list(mu = rep(2.5, 50)))  # base matrix() strips the advector class, so the tape sees constants # and the gradient is silently wrong. The check catches it. bad <- custom_family(   "bad", dpars = "mu", links = list(mu = "log"),   lpdf = function(y, dpars, aterms) {     m <- matrix(dpars$mu, ncol = 1)     y * log(m[, 1]) - m[, 1] - lgamma(y + 1)   },   type = "discrete" ) try(check_custom_family(bad, y = y, dpars = list(mu = rep(2.5, 50)))) #> Error : Failed to tape the lpdf: Invalid argument to 'advector' (lost class attribute?). Typical cause: base matrix()/c() stripping the advector class, or branching on parameter values

title: frmtmb: Formula-Based Regression Models via 'RTMB' — frmtmb-package
text: frmtmb implements established methods; introduces new estimator. Laplace approximation marginal likelihood latent-variable model, automatic differentiation, come 'TMB' / 'RTMB' (Kristensen et al. 2016). frmtmb generates objective; 'RTMB' differentiates integrates . formula grammar follows brms (Buerkner 2017). frmtmb frequentist implementation documented subset grammar. Formulas port brms without change. Random-effect syntax structured covariance vocabulary follow lme4 (Bates et al. 2015) glmmTMB (Brooks et al. 2017). Smooth terms built mgcv (Wood 2017, 2011) smoothCon() smooth2random(). Approximate Gaussian processes use Hilbert-space basis Riutort-Mayol et al. (2023). Spatial Gaussian Markov random fields use SPDE representation Lindgren et al. (2011) BYM2 parameterization Riebler et al. (2016). One-step-ahead residuals come Thygesen et al. (2017). Pooling across multiple imputations follows Rubin (1987) references given anova.frmtmb_multiple(). contribution architectural, statistical. Existing frequentist packages put formula front end one fixed likelihood; frmtmb compiles formula objective. makes several combinations ordinary code paths structural dead ends elsewhere: random effects distributional parameter, nonlinear predictors, per-response families multivariate model, monotonic effects, -model imputation, latent-class mixtures, custom families written plain R log-densities. vignette("compatibility") reports combinations supported, refused.

title: Solve an ODE once per group inside a nonlinear predictor — frm_ode
code: # One-compartment oral pharmacokinetics with between-subject # variability on the absorption and elimination rates. #   dA/dt = -ka A            A(0) = dose #   dC/dt =  ka A / V - ke C C(0) = 0 pk_dyn <- function(t, y, p) {   "c" <- RTMB::ADoverload("c")   list(c(-p[1] * y[1], p[1] * y[1] / p[3] - p[2] * y[2])) }  set.seed(2026) tt <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12) n_id <- 6 dd <- data.frame(id = factor(rep(seq_len(n_id), each = length(tt))),                  time = rep(tt, n_id), dose = 100) ka <- exp(rnorm(n_id, 0, 0.3))[as.integer(dd$id)] ke <- exp(rnorm(n_id, log(0.2), 0.25))[as.integer(dd$id)] dd$conc <- 100 * ka / (10 * (ka - ke)) *   (exp(-ke * dd$time) - exp(-ka * dd$time)) + rnorm(nrow(dd), 0, 0.3)  if (requireNamespace("RTMBode", quietly = TRUE)) {   # \donttest{   fit <- frm(     bf(conc ~ frm_ode(pk_dyn,                       init   = list(dose, 0),                       times  = time,                       parms  = list(exp(lka), exp(lke), exp(lV)),                       group  = id,                       states = c("depot", "central"),                       output = "central"),        lka ~ 1 + (1 | id), lke ~ 1 + (1 | id), lV ~ 1, nl = TRUE) +       gaussian(),     data = dd, start = list(beta = c(0, log(0.25), log(8))))   fixef(fit)   # }    # Repeated dosing: 100 into the depot every 12 hours. The dose at   # time 0 is the initial condition, the rest are events.   doses <- data.frame(time = c(12, 24, 36), state = "depot",                       value = 100)   frm_ode(pk_dyn, init = list(100, 0), times = c(6, 18, 30, 42),           parms = list(1, 0.2, 10), states = c("depot", "central"),           output = "central", events = doses) } #> [1] 3.733943 4.075490 4.106474 4.109285

title: Extract components of a fit, lme4 style — getME.frmtmb_fit
text: Supported names: "X" Fixed-effect design matrix mu predictor. "Z", "Zt" sparse random-effect design mu predictor transpose. Columns (rows Zt) span whole random-effect coefficient vector, block belonging another distributional parameter contributes zero columns . "beta", "fixef" primary (mu-family) fixed-effect coefficients, named. Coefficients auxiliary distributional parameters separate vector; use fixef() . "b" Conditional modes coefficient space, aligned columns Z. Reduced-rank (rr()) blocks expanded loadings, internal parameter vector. "theta" Covariance parameters internal (unconstrained) scale, confint(). lme4's relative-covariance-factor entries. "lower" Lower bounds theta. internal parameterization unbounded, vector -Inf, lme4's mixture 0 -Inf. Code tests theta == lower detect singular fit never fire; use diagnose() VarCorr() instead. "sigma" Residual standard deviation (sigma.frmtmb_fit()). "flist" grouping factors, one per distinct grouping variable. Smooth Gaussian-process blocks excluded: levels basis functions, groups. "assign" attribute. "n_rtrms", "n_rfacs" Number random-effect terms distinct grouping factors. Multivariate fits one design per response, "X", "Z" "Zt" need resp; names answer without .

code: set.seed(2) n <- 160 dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), g = factor(rep(1:16, 10))) u <- cbind(rnorm(16, 0, 0.8), rnorm(16, 0, 0.8)) e <- rnorm(n)                      # a disturbance both responses see dd$y1 <- 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 1] + e + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5) dd$y2 <- 2 - 0.3 * dd$x + u[dd$g, 2] + e + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)  # each response keeps its own formula and family fit <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x)) + gaussian(), data = dd) fixef(fit) #> $y1_mu #> (Intercept)           x  #>   1.0775542   0.5517536  #>  #> $y1_sigma #> (Intercept)  #>   0.2721586  #>  #> $y2_mu #> (Intercept)           x  #>   2.0235294  -0.2793594  #>  #> $y2_sigma #> (Intercept)  #>   0.2223223  #>   # rescor estimates the correlation of the residuals fit_rc <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x), rescor = TRUE) + gaussian(),               data = dd) rescor_matrix(fit_rc) #>           y1        y2 #> y1 1.0000000 0.6720766 #> y2 0.6720766 1.0000000  # set_rescor() turns it on after the fact, and `+` also combines bf()s mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x), bf(y2 ~ x)) + set_rescor(TRUE) #> y1 ~ x  #> y2 ~ x  #> rescor: TRUE  bf(y1 ~ x) + bf(y2 ~ x) #> y1 ~ x  #> y2 ~ x  #> rescor: FALSE   # |ID| correlates the random effects of the two responses fit_id <- frm(mvbf(bf(y1 ~ x + (1 | p | g)), bf(y2 ~ x + (1 | p | g))) +                 gaussian(), data = dd) VarCorr(fit_id) #>   y1 1 | g + y2 1 | g [ID]  #>               Name Std.Dev. y1.mu:(Intercept) #>  y1.mu:(Intercept)  0.86060                   #>  y2.mu:(Intercept)  0.61112             0.599

code: set.seed(1) dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), z = rnorm(100),                  g = factor(rep(1:10, 10))) dd$y <- rnorm(100, 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + rnorm(10, 0, 0.8)[dd$g], 1)  # `+` combines specifications; the class-wide one goes first so the # coefficient-specific one can override it pr <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b") +   set_prior("normal(0, 0.2)", class = "b", coef = "z") +   set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", group = "g") pr #> normal(0, 1) class=b #> normal(0, 0.2) class=b coef=z #> exponential(1) class=sd group=g  # the priors penalize the likelihood: the fit is a MAP estimate fit <- frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd, priors = pr) fixef(fit)$mu #> (Intercept)           x           z  #>  1.43922922  0.56382992  0.05323151  # the tight prior on z shrinks it toward zero fixef(frm(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd))$mu #> (Intercept)           x           z  #>  1.43901021  0.57150937  0.06947063   # an empty distribution string sets a hard bound only set_prior("", class = "b", coef = "x", lb = 0) #> (bounds only) class=b coef=x lb=0  # get_prior() shows which rows a design offers get_prior(bf(y ~ x + z + (1 | g)) + gaussian(), data = dd) #>    prior     class    coef group  dpar resp lb ub #> 1 (flat) Intercept                          NA NA #> 2 (flat)         b                          NA NA #> 3 (flat)         b       x                  NA NA #> 4 (flat)         b       z                  NA NA #> 5 (flat) Intercept               sigma      NA NA #> 6 (flat)        sd                          NA NA #> 7 (flat)        sd             g            NA NA #> 8 (flat)     theta                          NA NA #> 9 (flat)     theta theta_1                  NA NA

code: build_objective <- function(frame) {   lps       <- frame$linpreds   blocks    <- frame$re_blocks   block_nll <- lapply(blocks, \(bk) covstruct_registry[[bk$covstruct]]$nll)   fam_lpdf  <- lapply(frame$spec$responses, \(r) r$family$lpdf)   y         <- frame$y    function(pars) {     RTMB::getAll(pars, warn = FALSE)     "[<-" <- RTMB::ADoverload("[<-")     nll <- 0     for (bk in blocks)                       # loop over structure, not obs       nll <- nll - block_nll[[...]](b[bk$b_idx], theta[bk$theta_idx], bk$aux)     dparv <- list()     for (lp in lps) {       eta <- drop(lp$X %*% beta[lp$beta_idx])       if (!is.null(lp$Z))      eta <- eta + drop(lp$Z %*% b[lp$b_idx])       if (!is.null(lp$offset)) eta <- eta + lp$offset       dparv[[lp$key]] <- lp$link$inv(eta)     }     for (r in names(y)) {       yobs <- RTMB::OBS(y[[r]])              # free simulate() and OSA       nll  <- nll - sum(w[[r]] * fam_lpdf[[r]](yobs, dpars_for(r, dparv),                                                frame$spec$responses[[r]]$aterms))     }     nll   } }

New families: bernoulli, geometric, exponential, weibull (mean-parameterized, matches survreg’s likelihood), shifted_lognormal, hurdle_gamma, hurdle_lognormal, zero_inflated_binomial, zero_inflated_beta (validated glmmTMB), asym_laplace quantile regression (fixed quantile dpar reproduces quantreg::rq estimates). ranef(condVar = TRUE): conditional SDs modes (TMB/glmmTMB convention: fixed-effect uncertainty propagates), plus tidy .data.frame() methods ranef VarCorr output. frm_allfit(): refit every available optimizer (nlminb, optim, bobyqa, NLopt) compare, lme4 allFit() analog. frm_simulate(): de novo simulation bf() formula supplied parameters fitted model (power analysis; glmmTMB simulate_new() analog). frmtmb_control(profile = TRUE) (experimental): profile primary-coefficient vector inner Laplace problem, glmmTMBControl(profile = TRUE) / glmer(nAGQ = 0) speed approximation many-coefficient models; covariance comes joint precision. anova() longer fails models sharing primary formula (distributional vs plain fits); row labels now include dpar formulas.

title: frmtmb 0.13.0
text: Method-surface (“sugar”) milestone: conventional S3 methods downstream packages user muscle memory dispatch . New accessors: sigma(), terms(), weights(), model.matrix(), deviance(), extractAIC() (enables step() / drop1()), ngrps(), prior_summary(), profile() method wrapping TMB::tmbprofile(). Breaking: coef() now follows lme4 / glmmTMB / brms convention (per-group coefficients: fixed effects broadcast levels plus conditional modes). Use fixef() fixed effects alone. Fits without random effects still return coefficient vector. conditional_effects() base-graphics plot() method: grid predictions per predictor ("x:z" pair) Wald bands, smooths included, matrix covariates held column means. plot(fit): Pearson-residual diagnostics (residuals vs fitted, normal QQ). pp_check() (registered bayesplot generic): predictive checks simulate() draws ppc_* function. hypothesis(): tests arbitrary expressions parameters, brms spelling, three methods: delta-method Wald (default), "profile" (profile-likelihood intervals via TMB::tmbroot() lincombs; linear hypotheses, ML fits), "boot" (parametric bootstrap percentile intervals; expression). expression environment includes natural-scale random-effect names (sd_<group>__<term>, cor_<group>__<t1>__<t2>, sigma), ICC inference hypothesis(fit, "sd_g__Intercept^2 / (sd_g__Intercept^2 + sigma^2)", method = "boot"). result frmtmb_hypothesis data frame carrying bootstrap draws profile curves attributes, plot() method (bootstrap histogram, profile curve, implied Wald normal, per hypothesis). frm_bootstrap(fit, FUN, nsim): parametric bootstrap refit()s (bootMer analog), confint() percentile intervals. refit(fit, newresp): refit new response reusing assembled design warm start - one re-tape plus optimization; engine parametric bootstrap simulate() draws. accessor set makes insight’s default methods work (find_response(), get_data(), get_sigma(), n_obs(), …); dedicated insight methods (random-effect formula parts, get_parameters()) roadmap item.

title: frmtmb 0.12.0
text: Pre-release consolidation toward CRAN. Highlights milestone:

title: frmtmb 0.12.0
text: bf() distributional-parameter formulas carrying full predictor grammar (random effects smooths dpar), constant dpars, addition terms weights(), trials(), cens() (left / right / interval), trunc() (inclusive discrete correction). Nonlinear formulas (nl = TRUE) full linear predictor per parameter. Multivariate models: mvbf() / bf() + bf() / mvbind(), family per response, gaussian residual correlation (set_rescor()), |ID| random-effect correlation across formulas. mgcv smooths s() / t2() linear predictor, including matrix-covariate summation-convention terms: scalar--function, function--scalar, function--function regression validated mgcv. Covariance structures: us, diag, homdiag, cs, ar1, toep, ou (positions via num_factor()), known-structure terms gr(g, cov = ) (dense, correlated slopes via Kronecker product) gr(g, prec = Q) (sparse GMRF).

title: frmtmb 0.12.0
text: ML REML Laplace approximation; quadrature = TRUE upgrades scalar random effects adaptive Gauss-Kronrod marginalization (matches glmer(nAGQ = 25) GLMMadaptive). MAP / regularized ML via brms-style set_prior(); hard bounds (lower / upper, per-prior lb / ub). sdreport deferred standard errors first needed (roughly quarter fit time; se = TRUE restores eager mode). Pluggable optimizers (frmtmb_control(optimizer = )), including arbitrary user functions. confint() (Wald / profile / likelihood-root), natural-scale confint_varcorr(), anova() likelihood-ratio tests, diagnose().
